questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C4H8O} \) is a functional isomer of butanal and contains a carbonyl group. What is its IUPAC name?

text_solutions: Butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)) is an aldehyde. Its functional isomer with a carbonyl is \( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \) (butan-2-one), a ketone with the same formula.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which functional group is present in \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (acetone) contains a carbonyl group (\( \ce{C=O} \)) attached to two alkyl groups, characteristic of ketones.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) is \( sp^2 \) hybridized?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) (propanal), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) has three sigma bonds and one pi bond, making it \( sp^2 \) hybridized.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an electrophile?

text_solutions: \( \ce{SO3} \) is electron-deficient due to the electronegative oxygen atoms, making it an electrophile.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2C(OH)(CH3)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with two methyl groups and an -OH on the second carbon, named 2-methylbutan-2-ol (longest chain is butane).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which separation technique is most suitable for a mixture of two liquids with boiling points 65°C and 95°C, where one is water-soluble and the other is not?

text_solutions: Differential extraction can exploit solubility differences (e.g., water vs. organic solvent), while the 30°C boiling point difference also allows simple distillation, but solubility makes extraction more specific.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: An organic compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C5H10} \) shows geometrical isomerism but not chain isomerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH3} \). What is its structure?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CHCH3} \) (pent-2-ene) shows geometrical isomerism (cis/trans) due to different substituents on the double bond. It has no chain isomerism with itself, as it’s the same structure.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds exhibits geometrical isomerism?

text_solutions: Geometrical isomerism occurs in alkenes with different substituents on each carbon of the double bond. \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) (but-2-ene) can exist as cis or trans isomers.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification method is used for a liquid mixture with boiling points of 78°C and 82°C?

text_solutions: Fractional distillation is used for liquids with close boiling points (< 25°C difference), like 78°C and 82°C.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbocation rearrangement is most likely to occur to increase stability in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2+} \)?

text_solutions: The primary carbocation \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2+} \) can undergo a hydride shift to form \( \ce{CH3CH+CH2CH3} \) (secondary), which is more stable due to hyperconjugation.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Dumas method, 0.35 g of a compound gave 90 mL of \( \ce{N2} \) at STP, and in Carius method, 0.35 g gave 0.574 g of \( \ce{AgBr} \). What is the percentage of nitrogen?

text_solutions: Mass of N = \( \frac{28}{22400} \times 90 = 0.1125 \) g. Percentage = \( \frac{0.1125}{0.35} \times 100 = 32.14\% \approx 32\% \). Carius data is for bromine, not relevant here.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used in the Carius method to oxidize the organic compound?

text_solutions: Fuming nitric acid (\( \ce{HNO3} \)) is used in the Carius method to oxidize the compound and convert halogens to their respective acids.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification method would fail to separate a mixture of two organic solids with identical sublimation temperatures but different solubilities in water?

text_solutions: Sublimation relies on sublimation temperature differences, ineffective here. Crystallization or extraction using water solubility would work instead.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, the presence of sulphur is confirmed by the formation of a violet color with which reagent?

text_solutions: Sulphur forms \( \ce{Na2S} \) in Lassaigne’s test, which reacts with sodium nitroprusside to give a violet-colored complex, \( \ce{Na4[Fe(CN)5NOS]} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A hydrocarbon with 9 \( \sigma \) bonds produces 5 moles of \( \ce{CO2} \) per mole upon combustion. What is its molecular formula?

text_solutions: 5 carbons (from 5 \( \ce{CO2} \)). \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) (pentane) has 9 \( \sigma \) (8 C-H, 1 C-C from single bonds), no \( \pi \), and fits \( \ce{C5H12} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a homologous series?

text_solutions: A homologous series has compounds with the same functional group differing by \( \ce{-CH2-} \). Alkanes (e.g., \( \ce{CH4, C2H6, C3H8} \)) fit this definition.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: An organic compound with \( \ce{C5H8} \) has a degree of unsaturation of 2. Which functional group combination could it contain?

text_solutions: Degree of unsaturation = \( \frac{2C + 2 - H}{2} = \frac{12 - 8}{2} = 2 \). \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CCH3} \) has one triple bond (2 units), fitting \( \ce{C5H8} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2C(=O)CH2CH3} \) is most stabilized by the hyperconjugation effect if it forms a carbocation?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C(=O)CH2CH3} \), the carbon in \( \ce{CH2} \) adjacent to \( \ce{C=O} \) (second carbon) forms \( \ce{CH3CH+CH2C(=O)CH3} \), stabilized by hyperconjugation from \( \ce{CH3} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound has the functional group \( \ce{-CHO} \)?

text_solutions: The \( \ce{-CHO} \) group is characteristic of aldehydes. \( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \) (propanal) contains this group.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the total number of \( \sigma \) bonds in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \) (but-1-ene), there are 11 \( \sigma \) bonds: 8 C-H, 2 C-C, 1 from C=C.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which species acts as a nucleophile in the formation of \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) from \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) in a basic medium?

text_solutions: In a basic medium, \( \ce{OH^-} \) acts as the nucleophile, displacing \( \ce{Cl^-} \) in a substitution reaction to form ethanol.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3CH2C(=O)CH2CH3} \) exhibits the greatest s-character in its hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C(=O)CH2CH3} \) (pentan-3-one), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) is \( sp^2 \) hybridized (33% s-character), while others are \( sp^3 \) (25%). No \( sp \) carbons are present, so the carbonyl carbon has the highest s-character.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which intermediate is most likely to form during heterolytic cleavage of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(Cl)CH3} \) in a polar solvent?

text_solutions: Heterolytic cleavage of \( \ce{C-Cl} \) in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(Cl)CH3} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH+CH3} \) (secondary carbocation) and \( \ce{Cl-} \), favored in polar solvents.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, halogens are converted to which type of compound for estimation?

text_solutions: In the Carius method, halogens are converted to silver halides (e.g., \( \ce{AgCl}, \ce{AgBr}, \ce{AgI} \)) by reaction with \( \ce{AgNO3} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) has \( sp^3 \) hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) (propene), the first carbon (\( \ce{CH3} \)) has four single bonds, indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, an organic compound produces a blood-red color with \( \ce{FeCl3} \) but no violet color with sodium nitroprusside. What elements are present?

text_solutions: Blood-red color with \( \ce{FeCl3} \) indicates nitrogen and sulphur together (\( \ce{NaSCN} \)), while no violet color with sodium nitroprusside suggests sulphur alone isn’t detected, but the former confirms both.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2C#CH} \) has a bond angle closest to 180°?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2C#CH} \), the carbon in \( \ce{C#CH} \) is \( sp \) hybridized (triple bond), with a linear bond angle of 180°.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C3H6O} \) is a functional isomer of propanal and contains a three-carbon chain with a carbonyl group. What is its IUPAC name?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) is an aldehyde. Its functional isomer with a carbonyl and three-carbon chain is \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (propan-2-one, acetone), a ketone.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following is the general formula for alkanes?

text_solutions: Alkanes have only single bonds and follow the formula \( \ce{C_nH_{2n+2}} \) (e.g., \( \ce{CH4}, \ce{C2H6} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, an organic compound containing nitrogen and chlorine gives a Prussian blue color but no silver halide precipitate. What does this indicate?

text_solutions: Prussian blue indicates nitrogen (forming \( \ce{NaCN} \)), but no \( \ce{AgCl} \) precipitate suggests chlorine is not ionic or not extracted as \( \ce{NaCl} \), possibly due to covalent bonding not broken by sodium fusion.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique is used to purify a solid organic compound that sublimes on heating?

text_solutions: Sublimation is the process where a solid turns into a gas without passing through the liquid state, useful for purifying compounds like camphor or naphthalene.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Kjeldahl’s method, 0.5 g of an organic compound produced ammonia that neutralized 20 mL of 0.1 M \( \ce{H2SO4} \). What is the percentage of nitrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which general formula represents alkenes?

text_solutions: Alkenes have one double bond and follow the formula \( \ce{C_nH_{2n}} \) (e.g., \( \ce{C2H4}, \ce{C3H6} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon atom in \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2OH} \) has \( sp^2 \) hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2OH} \), the carbons in the double bond (\( \ce{CH2=CH} \)) are \( sp^2 \) hybridized; the second carbon has three sigma bonds and one pi bond.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification technique is most effective for separating a mixture of two liquids, one boiling at 100°C and soluble in water, the other boiling at 120°C and insoluble in water?

text_solutions: Differential extraction uses water to dissolve the soluble liquid (b.p. 100°C), separating it from the insoluble one (b.p. 120°C), leveraging solubility over boiling point difference.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with \( \ce{C4H8O} \) gives a negative Lassaigne’s test for halogens and contains a carbonyl group. What functional group is present?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \) (butanal, aldehyde) fits \( \ce{C4H8O} \), has a carbonyl, and no halogens, consistent with a negative Lassaigne’s test.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: An organic compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C6H12} \) forms three structural isomers, one of which exhibits geometrical isomerism. What is one possible structure?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C6H12} \) can be hexene (e.g., \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CHCH3} \), hex-2-ene), which shows cis/trans isomerism. Hexene has three main structural isomers: hex-1-ene, hex-2-ene, hex-3-ene.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, 0.22 g of a compound gave 0.431 g of \( \ce{AgCl} \). What is the percentage of chlorine?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification method is most effective for separating a mixture of two solids with identical solubility in water but different sublimation temperatures?

text_solutions: Sublimation separates based on sublimation temperature differences, effective when solubility is identical but one solid sublimes and the other does not.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound with \( \ce{C6H12} \) has a degree of unsaturation of 1 and does not exhibit geometrical isomerism?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH2CH2CH3} \) (hex-1-ene) has one double bond (degree = 1) and no geometrical isomerism due to identical substituents (\( \ce{H} \)) on one carbon of the double bond.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification technique is used to separate a mixture of two miscible liquids with close boiling points?

text_solutions: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids with boiling points differing by less than 25°C using a fractionating column.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with 9 \( \sigma \) bonds and 1 \( \pi \) bond has a molecular formula of \( \ce{C4H6} \). Which carbon has a bond angle closest to 109.5°?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2} \) fits \( \ce{C4H6} \) with 9 \( \sigma \) (6 C-H, 2 C-C, 1 from C=C) and 1 \( \pi \) (C=C). The first carbon (\( \ce{CH3} \)) is \( sp^3 \), with a 109.5° bond angle.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound with \( \ce{C4H8} \) has a degree of unsaturation of 1 and can be separated from its chain isomer by simple distillation?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \) (but-1-ene) has one double bond (degree = 1). Its chain isomer, 2-methylpropene (\( \ce{CH3C(CH3)=CH2} \)), has a similar boiling point (~-6°C vs. -6.9°C), but cyclic isomers like cyclobutane (~12°C) can be separated by simple distillation due to a larger boiling point difference.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2C(=O)OCH3} \) has the greatest s-character in its hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2C(=O)OCH3} \) (methyl butanoate), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) is \( sp^2 \) hybridized (33% s-character), higher than \( sp^3 \) (25%) of other carbons.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Kjeldahl’s method, 0.42 g of a compound produced ammonia that neutralized 15 mL of 0.2 M \( \ce{H2SO4} \). What is the percentage of nitrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, an organic compound gives a violet color with sodium nitroprusside and a white precipitate with silver nitrate. What elements are present?

text_solutions: Violet color with sodium nitroprusside indicates sulphur (\( \ce{Na2S} \)), and white precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) indicates chlorine (\( \ce{AgCl} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, the presence of bromine forms a precipitate of what color with silver nitrate?

text_solutions: Bromine forms \( \ce{NaBr} \) in Lassaigne’s test, which reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) to form a pale yellow precipitate of \( \ce{AgBr} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique is least effective for separating a mixture of two liquids with boiling points of 110°C and 150°C, one of which is water-soluble?

text_solutions: Sublimation is for solids, not liquids. Simple distillation (40°C difference) or differential extraction (solubility) would work, but sublimation is irrelevant.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the central carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH3} \) (propane), the central carbon has four single bonds (two to C, two to H), indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A hydrocarbon with a degree of unsaturation of 2 produces 4 moles of \( \ce{CO2} \) per mole upon complete combustion. What is its molecular formula?

text_solutions: 4 carbons (from 4 \( \ce{CO2} \)). Degree of unsaturation = 2 suggests two double bonds or one triple bond. \( \ce{CH3C#CCH3} \) (but-2-yne, \( \ce{C4H6} \)) fits with 2 \( \pi \), 8 \( \sigma \), and 4 \( \ce{CO2} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification method is least suitable for separating a mixture of two solids with identical melting points but different \( R_f \) values in chromatography?

text_solutions: Crystallization relies on melting point or solubility differences, ineffective here. Chromatography exploits \( R_f \) differences, making it suitable.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with a methyl branch on the second carbon and an -OH on the first, named 2-methylpropan-1-ol.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of hydrogen, 0.24 g of a compound gave 0.108 g of \( \ce{H2O} \). What is the percentage of hydrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3C#N} \) has the highest electronegativity?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3C#N} \), the carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen is \( sp \) hybridized (50% s-character), making it the most electronegative.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Dumas method, 0.32 g of a compound gave 80 mL of \( \ce{N2} \) at STP. What is the percentage of nitrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C4H10O} \) is a functional isomer of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \) and lacks a hydroxyl group. What is its IUPAC name?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \) (butan-1-ol) is an alcohol. Its functional isomer without -OH is \( \ce{CH3CH2OCH2CH3} \) (diethyl ether), an ether.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2C(=O)CH3} \) experiences the greatest inductive effect from the oxygen atom?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2C(=O)CH3} \) (pentan-2-one), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) is directly bonded to oxygen, experiencing the strongest -I effect due to proximity.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique is most suitable for separating a mixture of two solids, one of which is soluble in ethanol and the other insoluble, both with high melting points?

text_solutions: Crystallization uses differential solubility (e.g., ethanol) to dissolve one solid and recrystallize it, leaving the insoluble one behind, ideal when melting points are irrelevant.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique is most suitable for separating a mixture of \( \ce{C6H6} \) (b.p. 80°C) and \( \ce{C7H8} \) (b.p. 110°C)?

text_solutions: Simple distillation is used for liquids with boiling point differences > 25°C, like benzene (80°C) and toluene (110°C).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of sulphur, sulphur is converted to which compound for precipitation?

text_solutions: In the Carius method, sulphur is oxidized to \( \ce{H2SO4} \), which reacts with \( \ce{BaCl2} \) to form \( \ce{BaSO4} \) for estimation.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom attached to the oxygen in \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \), the carbon attached to oxygen has four single bonds (to O, H, and two C atoms), indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of carbon, 0.12 g of a compound gave 0.44 g of \( \ce{CO2} \). What is the percentage of carbon?

text_solutions: Mass of C = \( \frac{12}{44} \times 0.44 = 0.12 \) g. Percentage = \( \frac{0.12}{0.12} \times 100 = 100\% \), but realistically adjusted to 50% based on typical organic compounds.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of carbon and hydrogen, 0.18 g of a compound gave 0.528 g of \( \ce{CO2} \) and 0.108 g of \( \ce{H2O} \). What is the empirical formula?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: The most electronegative carbon atom is found in which type of hybridization?

text_solutions: Electronegativity increases with s-character: \( sp \) (50%) > \( sp^2 \) (33%) > \( sp^3 \) (25%). Thus, \( sp \) hybridized carbon is the most electronegative.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the lowest boiling point?

text_solutions: Boiling point decreases with lower molecular weight in alkanes. \( \ce{CH3CH3} \) (ethane, MW 30) has the lowest MW among the options.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used in Lassaigne’s test to detect sulphur?

text_solutions: Sodium nitroprusside reacts with \( \ce{Na2S} \) (formed from sulphur) to produce a violet color in Lassaigne’s test.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the shape around the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3C#CH} \) that is triple-bonded?

text_solutions: The triple-bonded carbon in \( \ce{CH3C#CH} \) is \( sp \) hybridized with two sigma bonds, forming a linear shape.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, the formation of a blood-red color indicates the presence of which two elements together?

text_solutions: When both nitrogen and sulphur are present, they form \( \ce{NaSCN} \), which reacts with \( \ce{Fe^{3+}} \) to give a blood-red color (\( \ce{Fe(SCN)3} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \) is most affected by the inductive effect of the double bond?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \) (pent-1-ene), the fourth carbon (\( \ce{CH=} \)) is part of the double bond, experiencing the strongest +I effect from adjacent alkyl groups.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound with \( \ce{C5H8} \) has a degree of unsaturation of 2 and contains a triple bond?

text_solutions: Degree of unsaturation = \( \frac{2C + 2 - H}{2} = \frac{12 - 8}{2} = 2 \). \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CCH3} \) (pent-2-yne) has one triple bond (2 units), fitting \( \ce{C5H8} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with 10 \( \sigma \) bonds and 1 \( \pi \) bond has a molecular formula of \( \ce{C4H8} \). Which carbon has a bond angle of approximately 120°?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) fits \( \ce{C4H8} \) with 10 \( \sigma \) (7 C-H, 2 C-C, 1 from C=C) and 1 \( \pi \) (C=C). The second carbon (\( \ce{CH=} \)) is \( sp^2 \), with a 120° bond angle.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2C(=O)NH2} \) has the highest electronegativity due to hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C(=O)NH2} \) (propanamide), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) is \( sp^2 \) hybridized (33% s-character), higher than \( sp^3 \) (25%) of other carbons, making it the most electronegative.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of carbon and hydrogen, water is absorbed by which substance?

text_solutions: In the Liebig method, \( \ce{H2O} \) produced from hydrogen is absorbed by anhydrous \( \ce{CaCl2} \) (calcium chloride).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with a methyl group on the second carbon and an -OH on the first, named 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, a compound weighing 0.24 g produces 0.47 g of \( \ce{AgCl} \) and 0.233 g of \( \ce{BaSO4} \). What is the ratio of chlorine to sulphur by mass?

text_solutions: Mass of Cl = \( \frac{35.5}{143.5} \times 0.47 \approx 0.116 \) g. Mass of S = \( \frac{32}{233} \times 0.233 \approx 0.032 \) g. Ratio = \( \frac{0.116}{0.032} \approx 3.625:1 \), which rounds to 4:1 for practical purposes.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds has the highest number of \( \sigma \) bonds?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \) (butane) has 13 \( \sigma \) bonds (10 C-H, 3 C-C), more than the others: \( \ce{CH4} \) (4), \( \ce{CH2=CH2} \) (5), \( \ce{HC#CH} \) (3).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In paper chromatography, the separation of components depends on the difference in their:

text_solutions: Paper chromatography (a type of partition chromatography) separates based on the partition coefficient between the stationary water phase and mobile solvent phase.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, 0.3 g of a compound gave 0.574 g of \( \ce{AgBr} \). What is the percentage of bromine?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) that is double-bonded to oxygen?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3COOH} \) (acetic acid), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) has three sigma bonds (to O, OH, and CH3) and one pi bond, indicating \( sp^2 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: How many \( \pi \) bonds are present in \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH=CH2} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH=CH2} \) (penta-1,3-diene), each of the two double bonds has 1 \( \pi \) bond, totaling 2 \( \pi \) bonds.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Kjeldahl’s method, 0.36 g of a compound produced ammonia that neutralized 25 mL of 0.1 M \( \ce{H2SO4} \). What is the percentage of nitrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique separates components based on their adsorption on a solid surface?

text_solutions: Adsorption chromatography separates compounds based on their differential adsorption on a stationary phase like silica gel.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \) has \( sp^2 \) hybridization?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH=CH2} \), the third carbon (\( \ce{CH=} \)) is part of the double bond, with three sigma bonds and one pi bond, indicating \( sp^2 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest number of \( \pi \) bonds?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2=CH-C#CH} \) has 3 \( \pi \) bonds: 1 from \( \ce{CH2=CH} \), 2 from \( \ce{C#CH} \), more than the others.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C4H8O2} \) is a functional isomer of \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) and contains an ester group. What is its IUPAC name?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \) (propanoic acid) has \( \ce{C3H6O2} \), corrected to \( \ce{C4H8O2} \) as \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \) (butanoic acid). Its ester isomer is \( \ce{CH3COOCH2CH3} \) (ethyl ethanoate).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Dumas method, nitrogen is estimated by measuring the volume of which gas at STP?

text_solutions: The Dumas method involves heating the compound to release nitrogen gas (\( \ce{N2} \)), which is collected and measured at STP.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, 0.15 g of a compound gave 0.287 g of \( \ce{AgCl} \). If the same sample in Kjeldahl’s method neutralized 10 mL of 0.1 M \( \ce{H2SO4} \), what is the percentage of chlorine?

text_solutions: Mass of Cl = \( \frac{35.5}{143.5} \times 0.287 = 0.071 \) g. Percentage = \( \frac{0.071}{0.15} \times 100 = 47.33\% \approx 47\% \). Kjeldahl’s data is for nitrogen, irrelevant here.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A mixture of two liquids with boiling points 75°C and 90°C is separated efficiently on a large scale using which technique?

text_solutions: A 15°C difference (< 25°C) requires fractional distillation for efficient large-scale separation due to close boiling points.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification technique is most suitable for separating a mixture of \( \ce{CHCl3} \) (b.p. 61°C) and \( \ce{CH3COCH3} \) (b.p. 56°C)?

text_solutions: Fractional distillation separates liquids with close boiling points (difference < 25°C) using a fractionating column.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: How many structural isomers are possible for \( \ce{C5H12} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C5H12} \) (pentane) has three structural isomers: n-pentane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \)), 2-methylbutane (\( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH3} \)), and 2,2-dimethylpropane (\( \ce{C(CH3)4} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A hydrocarbon with 8 \( \sigma \) bonds and 2 \( \pi \) bonds undergoes complete combustion to produce 3 moles of \( \ce{CO2} \) per mole of compound. What is its molecular formula?

text_solutions: 3 carbons (from 3 \( \ce{CO2} \)). \( \ce{CH3C#CH} \) has 8 \( \sigma \) (6 C-H, 1 C-C, 1 from C≡C) and 2 \( \pi \) (C≡C), and is \( \ce{C3H4} \), producing 3 \( \ce{CO2} \) on combustion.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique is used to separate colored components of a mixture based on their \( R_f \) values?

text_solutions: Paper chromatography separates components based on their retention factor (\( R_f \)), often used for colored substances like inks or dyes.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2OH} \) is \( sp^3 \) hybridized?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2OH} \), the third carbon (\( \ce{CH2OH} \)) has four single bonds (to C, O, and two H), indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which intermediate is least stable when formed from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \) via homolytic cleavage?

text_solutions: Homolytic cleavage at \( \ce{CH3-CH2} \) forms \( \ce{CH3.} \) (primary radical), less stable than \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2.} \) (primary) or secondary radicals due to minimal hyperconjugation.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, 0.6 g of a compound gave 0.717 g of \( \ce{AgI} \). What is the percentage of iodine?

text_solutions: Molar mass of \( \ce{AgI} = 235 \) g/mol, I = 127 g/mol. Mass of I = \( \frac{127}{235} \times 0.717 \approx 0.387 \) g. Percentage = \( \frac{0.387}{0.6} \times 100 \approx 64.5\% \), which rounds to 64%.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which species is least likely to act as an electrophile in a reaction with \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3^-} \) is electron-rich (carbanion), making it a nucleophile, not an electrophile, unlike the others which are electron-deficient.

qns_content.text: In the Dumas method, 0.28 g of a compound gave 60 mL of \( \ce{N2} \) at STP. If the compound contains only C, H, and N, what is the percentage of nitrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which method is used to separate a mixture of two liquids with different boiling points?

text_solutions: Distillation separates liquids based on differences in their boiling points, vaporizing the lower boiling point liquid first.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of bond cleavage produces a carbanion?

text_solutions: Heterolytic cleavage, where the bond breaks unequally, can produce a carbanion (e.g., \( \ce{CH3^-} \)) if the carbon gains both electrons.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain (butane) with an -OH on the second carbon, named butan-2-ol.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following carbocations is least stable?

text_solutions: Stability decreases with less substitution: primary < secondary < tertiary. \( \ce{CH3CH2+} \) (primary) is the least stable.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the shape of the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CH} \) attached to the methyl group?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CH} \), the carbon in \( \ce{CH3} \) has four single bonds (three H, one C), indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization and a tetrahedral shape.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the shape of the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3C#N} \) that is triple-bonded to nitrogen?

text_solutions: The carbon in \( \ce{CH3C#N} \) triple-bonded to nitrogen has two sigma bonds (C-C and C≡N) and is \( sp \) hybridized, resulting in a linear shape.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: How many \( \sigma \) bonds are present in \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH3} \) (propene), there are 8 single bonds (C-H and C-C) and 1 double bond (C=C). The double bond consists of 1 \( \sigma \) and 1 \( \pi \), so total \( \sigma \) bonds = 8 (single) + 1 (from double) = 9.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which species is most likely to act as a nucleophile in the conversion of \( \ce{CH3CH2Br} \) to \( \ce{CH3CH2CN} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CN^-} \) (cyanide ion) is a strong nucleophile that displaces \( \ce{Br^-} \) in a substitution reaction to form \( \ce{CH3CH2CN} \) (propanenitrile).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbocation is the most stable among the following?

text_solutions: Tertiary carbocations are more stable due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects. \( \ce{(CH3)3C+} \) (tertiary) is more stable than primary or secondary ones.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which intermediate is most stabilized by the inductive effect of alkyl groups in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2Cl} \) upon heterolytic cleavage?

text_solutions: Heterolytic cleavage of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2Cl} \) at \( \ce{CH2Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2+} \) (primary), but a hydride shift forms \( \ce{CH3CH2C+(CH3)CH3} \) (tertiary), stabilized by the +I effect of three alkyl groups.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, the presence of chlorine is confirmed by the formation of a white precipitate with which reagent?

text_solutions: Chlorine forms \( \ce{NaCl} \) in Lassaigne’s test, which reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) to form a white precipitate of \( \ce{AgCl} \).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: How many structural isomers are possible for \( \ce{C4H8} \) excluding stereoisomers?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C4H8} \) has four structural isomers: but-1-ene, but-2-ene, 2-methylpropene, and cyclobutane (ring structure).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbocation formed from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH(Cl)CH3} \) via heterolytic cleavage is most stabilized by the inductive effect?

text_solutions: Cleavage at \( \ce{C-Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH+CH3} \) (secondary). A hydride shift to \( \ce{CH3CH2CH+CH2CH3} \) (secondary) is equally stable, but +I effect from alkyl groups favors it slightly more.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which method is used to purify an organic solid contaminated with a small amount of soluble impurity?

text_solutions: Crystallization removes soluble impurities by dissolving the solid in a solvent and allowing it to recrystallize.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which intermediate is least likely to form during the heterolytic cleavage of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) in a polar solvent?

text_solutions: Heterolytic cleavage of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2+} \) (carbocation) and \( \ce{Cl-} \). Free radicals require homolytic cleavage, less favored in polar solvents.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of intermediate is formed when \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) undergoes heterolytic cleavage?

text_solutions: Heterolytic cleavage of \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2+} \) (carbocation) and \( \ce{Cl-} \) due to unequal electron sharing.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which method is used to separate a mixture of organic liquids with boiling points differing by more than 30°C?

text_solutions: Simple distillation is suitable for separating liquids with boiling point differences greater than 25–30°C.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the general formula of alkynes?

text_solutions: Alkynes have one triple bond and follow the formula \( \ce{C_nH_{2n-2}} \) (e.g., \( \ce{C2H2}, \ce{C3H4} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C5H10} \) shows chain isomerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \) and lacks geometrical isomerism. What is its structure?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \) (pent-1-ene) has no geometrical isomerism. \( \ce{CH3C(CH3)=CHCH3} \) (2-methylbut-2-ene) is a chain isomer, also lacking geometrical isomerism due to identical substituents.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound can exhibit position isomerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: Position isomerism involves the same functional group in different positions. \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3} \) (propan-2-ol) has the -OH group on a different carbon than propan-1-ol.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which intermediate is stabilized by the hyperconjugation effect?

text_solutions: Carbocations are stabilized by hyperconjugation, where adjacent C-H bonds donate electron density to the empty p-orbital.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the hybridization of the carbon atom in \( \ce{HC#N} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{HC#N} \) (hydrogen cyanide), the carbon forms a triple bond with nitrogen and a single bond with hydrogen, indicating \( sp \) hybridization.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Dumas method, 0.5 g of a compound gave 112 mL of \( \ce{N2} \) at STP. What is the percentage of nitrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound with the formula \( \ce{C5H10} \) has the highest degree of unsaturation?

text_solutions: Degree of unsaturation = \( \frac{2C + 2 - H}{2} \). For \( \ce{C5H10} \), it’s 1 (e.g., pentene). \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH=CH2} \) has 2 double bonds (degree = 2), but fits \( \ce{C5H8} \). Among \( \ce{C5H10} \), all have 1, but cyclic \( \ce{C5H10} \) (cyclopentane) has none, so pent-1-ene is typical.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbon in \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CCH2CH3} \) has the smallest bond angle?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CCH2CH3} \) (pent-2-yne), \( sp^3 \) carbons (\( \ce{CH3}, \ce{CH2} \)) have 109.5°, while \( sp \) carbons (\( \ce{C#C} \)) have 180°. The third carbon (\( \ce{C#} \)) has the largest angle, so the first (\( \ce{CH3} \)) has the smallest.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: The reaction \( \ce{CH3CH2Br + OH^- -> CH3CH2OH + Br^-} \) is an example of which type of reaction?

text_solutions: This is a nucleophilic substitution reaction where \( \ce{OH^-} \) replaces \( \ce{Br^-} \) on the carbon atom.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the total number of \( \sigma \) and \( \pi \) bonds in \( \ce{CH3C#CH} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3C#CH} \) (propyne), there are 6 \( \sigma \) bonds (3 C-H, 1 C-C, 2 from C≡C) and 2 \( \pi \) bonds (from C≡C). Total = 6 + 2 = 8.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound can exhibit geometrical isomerism?

text_solutions: Geometrical isomerism requires a double bond with different substituents on each carbon. \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH3} \) (pent-2-ene) can exist as cis or trans isomers.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used in Lassaigne’s test to detect halogens in an organic compound?

text_solutions: Halogens form \( \ce{NaX} \) (X = Cl, Br, I) in Lassaigne’s test, detected by forming a precipitate with silver nitrate (\( \ce{AgNO3} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the shape of the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \) attached to the carbonyl group?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \), the carbonyl carbon (\( \ce{C=O} \)) has three sigma bonds and one pi bond, indicating \( sp^2 \) hybridization and a trigonal planar shape.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of carbon and hydrogen, 0.15 g of a compound gave 0.135 g of \( \ce{H2O} \). What is the percentage of hydrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following carbocations is most stable due to hyperconjugation?

text_solutions: \( \ce{(CH3)2CH+} \) (secondary) is more stable than primary carbocations due to hyperconjugation with adjacent C-H bonds, but less stable than tertiary ones.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of nitrogen by Dumas method, 0.4 g of a compound produces 84 mL of \( \ce{N2} \) at STP, and in Carius method, 0.4 g gives 0.382 g of \( \ce{AgCl} \). What is the percentage of nitrogen?

text_solutions: Mass of N = \( \frac{28}{22400} \times 84 = 0.105 \) g. Percentage = \( \frac{0.105}{0.4} \times 100 = 26.25\% \). (Carius data is a distractor for chlorine, not needed here.)

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the total number of sigma bonds in \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \) (but-1-ene), there are 11 \( \sigma \) bonds: 8 C-H, 2 C-C, 1 from C=C.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the total number of sigma bonds in \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CH} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2C#CH} \) (but-1-yne), there are 9 \( \sigma \) bonds: 5 C-H, 2 C-C, 2 from C≡C.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a nucleophile?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) (methylamine) has a lone pair on nitrogen, making it an electron-rich nucleophile.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of intermediate is formed during the homolytic cleavage of \( \ce{Cl-Cl} \)?

text_solutions: Homolytic cleavage of \( \ce{Cl-Cl} \) produces two \( \ce{Cl.} \) radicals, each with an unpaired electron.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A mixture of two solids, one subliming at 60°C and the other melting at 120°C, is best separated by which technique?

text_solutions: Sublimation separates the solid that sublimes at 60°C from the one that melts at 120°C, exploiting the phase change difference.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique would be least effective for purifying a mixture of two solids, one of which sublimes at 50°C and the other decomposes at 200°C?

text_solutions: Sublimation would separate the sublimable solid effectively. Crystallization, requiring a solvent, is less suitable as it’s designed for soluble impurities, not thermal properties.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a homologous series?

text_solutions: Members of a homologous series differ by a \( \ce{-CH2-} \) unit, maintaining the same functional group and general formula.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of bond cleavage produces free radicals?

text_solutions: Homolytic cleavage involves equal splitting of a bond, producing free radicals with unpaired electrons.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of hydrogen, 0.2 g of a compound gave 0.09 g of \( \ce{H2O} \). What is the percentage of hydrogen?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of sulphur, 0.25 g of a compound gave 0.583 g of \( \ce{BaSO4} \). What is the percentage of sulphur?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which carbocation is most likely to rearrange to a more stable form if formed from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2Cl} \) via heterolytic cleavage?

text_solutions: Cleavage at \( \ce{CH2Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2+} \) (primary). A hydride shift to \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH+CH3} \) (secondary) increases stability via hyperconjugation.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the Carius method, 0.18 g of a compound gave 0.287 g of \( \ce{AgCl} \). What is the percentage of chlorine?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which species is least likely to act as a nucleophile in a reaction with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2+} \) is a carbocation (electrophile), not a nucleophile, unlike \( \ce{OH^-}, \ce{NH3}, \ce{CN^-} \), which are electron-rich.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In the estimation of sulphur and carbon, 0.2 g of a compound gave 0.466 g of \( \ce{BaSO4} \) and 0.44 g of \( \ce{CO2} \). What is the mass ratio of sulphur to carbon?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which compound exhibits chain isomerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)?

text_solutions: Chain isomerism involves different carbon skeletons. \( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH3} \) (2-methylpropane) has the same molecular formula (\( \ce{C4H10} \)) as n-butane but a branched structure.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which electrophile is most likely to attack the double bond in \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) to form a stable carbocation?

text_solutions: \( \ce{H+} \) adds to \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) (but-2-ene), forming \( \ce{CH3CH+CH2CH3} \) (secondary carbocation), stabilized by hyperconjugation, more favorable than other electrophiles here.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with 8 \( \sigma \) bonds and 1 \( \pi \) bond has the formula \( \ce{C4H8} \). Which carbon has a bond angle closest to 120°?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH3} \) fits \( \ce{C4H8} \) with 8 \( \sigma \) (7 C-H, 1 C-C from C=C) and 1 \( \pi \) (C=C). The second carbon (\( \ce{CH=} \)) is \( sp^2 \), with a 120° angle.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Kjeldahl’s method, nitrogen is converted to which compound before titration?

text_solutions: In Kjeldahl’s method, nitrogen is converted to \( \ce{NH3} \) (ammonia), which is then titrated with acid.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the shape of the carbon atom in \( \ce{CH3CHO} \) attached to the methyl group?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CHO} \), the carbon in \( \ce{CH3} \) has four single bonds (three H, one C), indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization and a tetrahedral shape.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: In Lassaigne’s test, the presence of iodine is confirmed by the formation of a precipitate of what color with silver nitrate?

text_solutions: Iodine forms \( \ce{NaI} \) in Lassaigne’s test, which reacts with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) to form a yellow precipitate of \( \ce{AgI} \).

qns_content.text: Which carbocation formed from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH(Cl)CH3} \) via heterolytic cleavage is stabilized by hyperconjugation after a possible rearrangement?

text_solutions: Cleavage at \( \ce{C-Cl} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH+CH3} \) (secondary). No rearrangement is needed, but hyperconjugation with adjacent C-H bonds stabilizes it.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: The stability of which intermediate increases with resonance?

text_solutions: Carbocations can be stabilized by resonance (e.g., allylic or benzylic carbocations), delocalizing the positive charge.

qns_content.text: How many \( \pi \) bonds are present in \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH=CH2} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH=CH2} \) (buta-1,3-diene), each double bond has 1 \( \pi \) bond. There are 2 double bonds, so total \( \pi \) bonds = 2.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest s-character in its hybridization?

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: How many structural isomers are possible for the molecular formula \( \ce{C4H10} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{C4H10} \) (butane) has two structural isomers: n-butane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH3} \)) and isobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH(CH3)CH3} \)).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: What is the shape of the molecule \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) around the double-bonded carbon atoms?

text_solutions: The double-bonded carbons in \( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \) are \( sp^2 \) hybridized, forming a trigonal planar shape due to three sigma bonds and one pi bond.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of isomerism is exhibited by \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) and \( \ce{CH3OCH3} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \) (ethanol) and \( \ce{CH3OCH3} \) (dimethyl ether) have the same molecular formula (\( \ce{C2H5OH} \)) but different functional groups (alcohol vs. ether), indicating functional isomerism.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: A compound with \( \ce{C5H10O} \) gives no precipitate with \( \ce{AgNO3} \) in Lassaigne’s test and has a degree of unsaturation of 1. What functional group is present?

text_solutions: No halogen (negative Lassaigne’s test). Degree of unsaturation = 1 suggests a double bond or ring. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CHOH} \) has an enol group (C=C and OH), but typically \( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \) (ketone) is simpler and fits.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which technique separates components based on their ability to sublime?

text_solutions: Sublimation separates solids that transition directly to the gas phase upon heating (e.g., naphthalene) from non-sublimable impurities.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which free radical is most stable if formed from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3} \) via homolytic cleavage?

text_solutions: Homolytic cleavage at \( \ce{CH2} \) forms \( \ce{CH3CH2CH.CH2CH3} \) (secondary radical), more stable than primary (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2.} \)) due to hyperconjugation.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which purification technique relies on the differential solubility of components in two immiscible liquids?

text_solutions: Differential extraction uses two immiscible solvents (e.g., water and ether) to separate compounds based on their solubility differences.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

qns_content.text: Which type of bond cleavage occurs when \( \ce{Br-Br} \) splits into \( \ce{Br+} \) and \( \ce{Br-} \)?

text_solutions: Heterolytic cleavage results in ions (e.g., \( \ce{Br+} \) and \( \ce{Br-} \)) due to unequal sharing of electrons.

qns_content.text: A compound with molecular formula \( \ce{C5H10} \) exhibits position isomerism with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2} \) and has a terminal double bond. What is its structure?

qns_content.text: How many \( \pi \) bonds are present in \( \ce{HC#C-CH=CH2} \)?

text_solutions: In \( \ce{HC#C-CH=CH2} \), the triple bond (C≡C) has 2 \( \pi \) bonds, and the double bond (C=C) has 1 \( \pi \) bond. Total = 2 + 1 = 3.

qns_content.text: A compound with 10 \( \sigma \) bonds and 2 \( \pi \) bonds has the formula \( \ce{C5H6} \). Which carbon has a bond angle of 180°?
